name: Saint Hyacinth
history: A Polish Dominican who received the habit in the first years of the order and carried its preaching across Poland and far to the north and east. He founded houses of friars in Kraków and beyond and was called the apostle of the North. He died in Kraków on the feast of the Assumption, 1257.
life: Jacek Odrowąż was a priest of a noble Silesian family. Around 1220 he went to Rome with his bishop and there, tradition holds, received the habit of the Friars Preachers from Saint Dominic himself. Returning to Poland, he founded the Dominican house of the Holy Trinity in Kraków and others in Gdańsk and further afield. He preached in Poland, Prussia and among the peoples of the eastern lands, travelling enormous distances on foot. Many stories gathered around him. The best known says that when the Tatars attacked Kyiv he rescued the Blessed Sacrament from the church and, hearing Our Lady ask not to be left behind, carried off her heavy statue as well, which became light in his arms. He had a great love for the Mother of God and died, fittingly, on the day of her Assumption. He was canonised in 1594.
prayerTo: Saint Hyacinth, tireless preacher, you carried Christ and His Mother to people who had not heard of them. Pray for missionaries, for Poland, and for all who travel for the sake of the Gospel. When I am in danger, help me to keep hold of what matters most. Amen.
penance: Walk somewhere today instead of driving, praying as you go for missionaries and for the conversion of those who do not know Christ.
meditation: The story says the statue of Our Lady became light when he lifted it. Which burden might become lighter if you carried it with her?
prayer: O God, Who, year by year, dost gladden us by the solemn feast-day of thy blessed confessor Hyacínthi, mercifully grant unto all who keep his birthday, grace to follow after the pattern of his godly conversation. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
